verdict.rationale: The agent controls the whole iPhone OS rather than one walled app. It drives an AssistiveTouch pointer through the ESP32 acting as a mouse, and the docs show it leaving its own app to open Clock, type a time and save. However, the target is iOS apps, not desktop applications, and keyboard-shortcut support is never documented. Missing for 10: desktop-OS application control, keyboard shortcuts, and independent hands-on corroboration of cross-app reliability.

support.subject: As a power user, the agent operates desktop applications (click, type, keyboard shortcuts) across the whole OS, not one walled app

citations.quote: the agent leaves its own app, opens Clock, types the time into the wheel, ticks the days and saves.
The board is now the AirPlay receiver and the mouse, and the agent runs in an iPhone app on the same phone.
Let Me Use the Pointer — turn on AssistiveTouch; the app calibrates the pointer by itself.
